article.title: Democrats Won
article.author: Chuck Yates
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. I was pretty depressed when Donald Trump won a second term in 2024, and Republicans secured control of both houses. I knew life was about to get really awful for a lot of people. But I also knew that it was the midterm election in 2026 would determine just how awful, how depressing. Now that election is over, and the big blue wave the pollsters and pundits promised has washed away the MAGA majority, the United States will be in the care of lawmakers who will prefer principle over party and people over politics—or so we may hope. Here in Idaho, with five Republican voters for every Democrat, it’s no surprise that everything stayed bright red. Republican incumbents were reelected, and voters agreed to amend the state constitution to make English the official language. Somewhat surprisingly, they rejected a proposed constitutional amendment that would have given the legislature exclusive authority to regulate marijuana and other psychoactive substances. Proposition 1, The Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act, failed, but not spectacularly for this state, where the existing Defense of Life Act prohibits abortion except to save the life of the mother, and in cases of rape and incest, and only in the first trimester. The new law would have retained essentially the same restrictions, but it would have decriminalized both the procedure and the medical professionals who perform it. As it is, Idaho abortion law remains more committed to punishing evildoers than to defending the lives of unborn children. Related: Voting for the Future of America In other words, not much will change here in Idaho. And now that the state’s voters have chosen the Winchester Model 1873 as Idaho’s official state firearm—no kidding—demand for that rifle likely will surge, as Idahoans line up to spend nearly $3700 for the 150th anniversary commemorative edition of “The Gun that Won the West.” They’ll want to add John Wayne’s weapon of choice to their home arsenals, but of course it won’t displace their AR-15s and other military hardware. A true Idaho patriot needs at least one assault rifle. Nationally, though, the possibilities are tantalizing for all who value human dignity and decency. Air Force Major Jason Watson may be vindicated in his call for impeachment, conviction, and removal, even if the military justice system will end his career and probably his personal freedom as well. Major Watson is the poster child for the conflict between obedience and conscience. At the time of his arrest, I wrote, “We need more patriots like Major Jason Watson, willing to serve their country by defying their superiors and falling on their swords to prove their sincerity.” Related: What I Learned in Nagasaki: We Are Not Innocent When We Look Away A less Islamophobic Congress may act to end the pointless and wasteful war with Iran. They may restore sovereignty and self determination to the people of Venezuela. They may even take steps to end the slaughter in Gaza and the West Bank. And immigrants may be able, again, to live without having to worry about roving gangs of ICE and Border Patrol thugs. Who knows? We might even see criminal prosecutions for the members of those gangs who’ve murdered innocent Americans exercising their right to “petition the Government for a redress of grievances.” However, the newly elected Democratic majority won’t take office for another two months. In that interval, Trump and his myrmidons will be able to continue their assault on immigrants, on public and protected lands, on randomly chosen enemies foreign and domestic, on the Constitution and the laws of the land, and on the values that informed those “self evident truths” at the moment of the country’s founding. Unregulated mining, drilling, and logging will continue in former national monuments, in national forests, and on BLM lands. The border wall will continue to grow between the US and Mexico, with bulldozers in national parks and backhoes in cultural and historic sites. Air and water will remain threatened by the pollution of rampant development, and endangered species will continue to live without protection, hunted for trophies and crowded into shrinking habitat by subdivisions and shopping malls. Related: Controlling Unalienable Rights in Idaho The midterm election has given us a genuine hope of seeing that morning in America that Ronald Reagan used to talk about. The United States may soon return to the high ideals of its founding documents. But to honor the metaphor, we have to acknowledge that, despite the faint hint of a coming sunrise, the night is not over yet, and dawn may break over the ruined landscape of a once-proud republic awaiting our commitment to restore it. The hard work has only just begun. As Martin Luther King, Jr. once remarked, “We stand in life at midnight; we are always on the threshold of a new dawn.” And most famously, he said, “I say to you today, my friends, that in spite of the difficulties and frustrations of the moment, I still have a dream.” We must resolve to dream with him, and to hold fiercely to that hope.
